title: CLI approve command — `npx pp approve <id>` from terminal without leaving the IDE
description: Marco lives in the terminal. Add a lightweight CLI command to the PP npm package that lets developers approve a pending deploy request without opening a browser. `npx @permissionprotocol/sdk approve <requestId>` authenticates via stored API key, shows a 3-line summary (repo, PR#, risk), and confirms with Y/n. This closes the loop entirely inside the developer's workflow. Files: new CLI entry point in the SDK package (packages/sdk/src/cli.ts) + approve API endpoint if not already exposed.
archived_reason: Premature: CLI approve is niche, browser/URL works. Revisit after 10+ active users.

title: Approval velocity dashboard — time-to-approve metrics per repo
description: Sarah needs compliance evidence that approvals aren't rubber-stamped. Add a simple metrics section to the dashboard showing: average time-to-approve (last 7d/30d), approval rate, and a sparkline of daily approval counts per repo. Pull from existing deploy request timestamps. This turns PP from a gate into an audit tool — the data that proves the process works. Files: new metrics API route (src/app/api/pp/metrics/route.ts) + dashboard component.
archived_reason: Premature: metrics dashboard before users is vanity metrics. Revisit after 10+ active users.

title: Auto-approve rules engine — skip human review for low-risk, auto-gate high-risk
description: Not every deploy needs a human. Add a rules config (pp.config.json or env vars) where teams define auto-approve criteria: e.g. only docs/test files changed, PR author is in trusted list, or staging environment. High-risk changes (migrations, auth, env vars) always require human approval. This makes PP invisible for routine work and loud for dangerous work — exactly what Marco wants. Files: new rules evaluation in the verify route + config schema + docs.
archived_reason: Premature: auto-approve rules need user feedback on what patterns matter. Revisit after dogfooding.

title: Team routing — auto-assign approver based on changed file paths
description: When a PR touches /src/auth/*, route the approval to the security team lead. When it touches /migrations/*, route to the DBA. Add a routing config (pp-routing.yml in the repo root) that maps glob patterns to approver emails/GitHub handles. The approval page shows who was assigned and why. Sarah gets the right eyes on the right code; Marco doesn't get pinged for stuff outside his domain. Files: new routing config parser + approver assignment in verify route + approval page display.
archived_reason: Premature: team routing is enterprise. Need single-approver flow proven first.

title: Multi-approver policy — require N-of-M approvals for production deploys
description: Production deploys by AI agents shouldn't rest on one person. Add a policy config where teams set approval thresholds: e.g. 2-of-3 for production, 1-of-1 for staging. The approval page shows progress (1/2 approved, waiting on Sarah). This is the feature enterprise security teams expect before adopting any gate. Files: policy config schema + approval counting logic in verify route + approval page progress UI.
archived_reason: Premature: multi-approver is enterprise. Need single-approver adoption first.

title: Auto-expire stale deploy requests with PR comment notification
description: Deploy requests older than TTL silently expire — the developer never knows. Add a cleanup worker (or cron in the existing embedded worker) that posts a GitHub PR comment when a request expires: 'This deploy request expired after 24h without approval. Push a new commit to trigger a fresh request.' Keeps the queue clean and gives Marco a clear recovery path. Files: worker/cleanup logic + GitHub PR comment integration.
archived_reason: System hygiene feature, less critical for initial user acquisition and core flow completion.

title: Webhook events on approve/deny — let teams build custom integrations
description: Fire a configurable webhook POST on every approval or denial event. Payload: request ID, repo, PR, approver, decision, receipt URL, timestamp. Teams can pipe this into PagerDuty, Datadog, their own Slack bots, audit systems. This makes PP an event source, not just a gate. One env var: PP_WEBHOOK_URL. Files: new webhook dispatcher utility + hook into approval/denial flow.
archived_reason: Premature for initial user acquisition; focuses on advanced integration rather than core flow or first-time user experience.

title: Approval timeline on receipt proof page — full chain-of-custody visualization
description: The UAR proof page should tell the whole story. Add a vertical timeline showing: request created (with commit SHA) → gate blocked CI → human opened review → approved/denied (with approver identity) → deploy proceeded. Sarah needs this for audit evidence. Pull timestamps from the existing deploy request record. File: the receipt/proof page component (src/app/pp/receipts/[id]/page.tsx or equivalent).
archived_reason: Enhances the post-approval receipt, but less critical for the immediate goal of getting agents through the gate and users to complete the flow.

title: Embeddable approval badge — live SVG status for README and dashboards
description: Like CI badges but for authorization. A live SVG badge (shields.io style) showing 'PP: Approved ✓' or 'PP: Pending Review' that teams embed in repo READMEs, Notion docs, or internal dashboards. Clicking the badge opens the receipt proof page. This is free marketing — every repo that uses PP advertises it in their README. Files: new badge API route (src/app/api/pp/badge/[requestId]/route.ts) returning SVG.
archived_reason: Less critical for initial adoption and core mission success metrics; more of a 'brand polish' or 'advanced integration' item.

title: Emergency bypass with escalated audit trail — break glass, but on the record
description: Sometimes production is down and you can't wait for approval. Add a 'break glass' emergency bypass that lets a deploy proceed immediately but creates an escalated audit record: who bypassed, why (required reason), timestamp, and flags the receipt as EMERGENCY_BYPASS. Post-incident, this is the evidence that the bypass was justified. Config: PP_EMERGENCY_BYPASS_ALLOWED=true + list of authorized bypassers. Files: bypass endpoint + emergency receipt type + bypass UI button (hidden behind confirmation modal).
archived_reason: More of an advanced operational feature, less critical for initial user acquisition and perfecting the core AI agent deploy-gate flow.

title: Receipt signature in PR merge commit — cryptographic proof baked into git history
description: When a PP-approved PR merges, append the UAR signature hash to the merge commit message as a Git trailer: `PP-Receipt: sha256:abc123...`. This means the authority proof lives permanently in git history — any auditor can verify authorization was granted by checking the commit. No dashboard needed. Files: GitHub webhook listener for merge events + commit amendment via API (or merge commit message template).
archived_reason: While important for auditability, the core receipt link is already handled by an immune idea. This is a deeper integration and less critical for initial user experience or acquisition.

title: Display related CI workflow status on approval page
description: Integrate the status of the associated GitHub Actions workflow run (e.g., `CI Status: ✅ Passed`) into the approval screen, perhaps within the `Context` or `Assessment` zone (e.g., `app/components/approval-screen/context-zone.tsx`). This provides immediate visibility into other CI checks for both Marco and Sarah, fetching data via the GitHub API.
archived_reason: Off-FOCUS: Provides context that can be found elsewhere (GitHub). Less critical for the core approval decision than other approval screen improvements, and can be deferred.

title: Slack webhook notification on gate block — with approve link
description: Most engineering teams live in Slack. When deploy-gate blocks a PR, fire a webhook to a configurable Slack incoming webhook URL with a formatted message: repo, PR title, risk summary, and a direct approve link. Configuration via env var PP_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL on the app. This is the 'meet developers where they are' play — they see the block in Slack, click approve, done. Files: new notification utility + hook into the verify/gate-failure flow.
archived_reason: Off-FOCUS: External notification, not part of the core UI/approval flow. While useful, it's not critical for the initial end-to-end flow or user acquisition, and can be implemented later or addressed by other means.

title: Deny-with-reason flow — require explanation on rejection, post to PR
description: When Sarah denies a deploy request, she should be forced to say why. Add a required 'reason' text field to the deny action, then post that reason as a GitHub PR comment with a clear 'Deploy Denied' badge. The developer immediately knows what to fix without asking. This closes the feedback loop on denials — currently they're a dead end. Files: deny endpoint enhancement + PR comment integration + approval page deny form update.
archived_reason: Off-FOCUS: Less critical for the initial mission of getting AI agents to deploy *through* PP. Focus is on successful approval flow first; denial feedback can be iterated on later.

title: Environment-specific quick approval button
description: Add a context-aware "Approve for [Environment]" button (e.g., "Approve for Staging") to the `Action` zone of the approval screen (e.g., `app/components/approval-screen/action-zone.tsx`). This button would appear above the fold, leveraging the environment theming and allowing Marco to approve routine deploys with a single click without scrolling or additional input.
archived_reason: Off-FOCUS: Convenience feature, not critical for the initial end-to-end flow or user acquisition. Can be added in an iteration once the core approval process is solid.

title: AI Agent PR Context in GitHub Action Output
description: Enhance the `deploy-gate.yml` GitHub Action to detect PRs from known AI agents (e.g., `github-actions[bot]`, `codex-bot`). When a gate blocks an AI agent's PR, modify the `app/actions/github-gate/run.js` output to prominently display "🤖 AI Agent PR: Requires Permission Protocol approval." This provides immediate context for Marco in the CI logs.
archived_reason: Duplicate: overlaps significantly with idea-004 (Rich gate-failure CI output), which is higher priority and can incorporate AI agent context.

title: PR comment with receipt link + 1-line AI summary on auto-approved PRs
description: Deploy-gate v2 creates a request for every PR. Auto-approved ones should get a PR comment showing the receipt link and a 1-line AI-generated summary of what changed. This is the product touchpoint — developers see PP on every PR without friction. Add a GitHub PR comment step to the post-approval flow in the verify route, using the existing AI summary from the deploy request.
